newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Harried Australia dlr takes comfort in RBA silence.
newsitem.headline: Harried Australia dlr takes comfort in RBA silence.

text.p: A harried Australian dollar found a moments peace atop 75 cent support at the midsession as an uneasy calm settled on the market after the Reserve Bank declined to cut rates as some impatient speculators had hoped.

With little data due in the next fortnight there was no obvious trigger for a move until the RBA's board meeting on July 1. But that did not mean the market could relax given the bank had caught it napping with three of the four cuts this cycle.
This sort of uncertain atmosphere was not going to be conducive to a dollar recovery and dealers looked for a test of 75 cents soon with a real risk of seeing US$.7450 and beyond.
By 12.15 pm (0215 GMT) the dollar was settling into its new home at US$0.7514/19 having marked out a US$0.7505/7530 range since tumbling from US$0.7570 in the wake of Thursday's dire jobs data.

It was a cent down on the week and almost three cents off from the US$0.7780 level held before the RBA last cut rates on May 23. Chart watchers had turned decidedly bearish following the break of US$0.7550, which had previously been the 1997 low, and saw little to prevent the downtrend extending to the 1996 trough of 73 cents in the medium term. The recapture of US$0.7550 was the minimum needed to forestall this scenario.
On the crosses the currency continued to track every tremor in US$/yen, although this was also quiet today after Thursday's wild four yen rally, and it stood at 85.84/94 yen from 85.74/84.
In trade weighted terms it was steady at 57.1.

The money market was clearly gunning for an easing with the September 90-day bank bill futures contract aty 94.90, implying a rate of 5.10 percent against the present 5.50 percent cash rate. A$ forwards out to three years were now trading at a premium meaning it cost exporters to hedge forward, which could be one reason why corporates were keen to take cover in the sport market. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
